chapter: Benny Goodman and first US jobs
title: Louis Armstrong's 'Bop Chops' and his first US job with Charlie Parker
summary: Armstrong greeted him as Bop Chops; his first American gig was with the Charlie Parker All-Stars on the Dinah Washington show at the Earle Theater.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Okay, we’ll take a break right there. We’re gonna change--
And in theater, Louis Armstrong came to [unintelligible] [laughs] and listen to us.
So you got to meet him and this is when he called you a…

[And sure I went Mr.] [inaudible] [to present Myers?]. “How ya doin’ Bop Chops?” Yeah, that’s... Well, that’s [stammers]. You cannot erase those memories, you know. And Charlie Parker. That was before. I played with Charlie Parker at the Earl Theater in the Dinah Washington. That was the queen of the blues—Dinah Washington. And also featuring, you know, Charlie Parker All-Stars with Miles and Bags. Me and Beryl Booker was the pianist. She was good. She was the accompanist for Dinah and Jimmy Cobb, who was more than any accompanist who worked for Dinah. [laughs]
That’s in ’50. That was my first job in the States.
And then the day… No, with Charlie Parker.
…was your first gig in the States.
